summary: Orbe is a WebXR mixed reality platform designed with the PICO 4 Ultra headset that transforms climate visual data into polyphonic soundscapes and tactile landscapes without the need for downloads. Addressing "The Earth Information Jukebox" challenge, it uses real-time acoustic ecology, responsive 3D modeling, and haptic feedback to translate critical Earth data into an 100% original and accessible experience. Instead of relying on traditional visual dashboards that suffer from spatial occlusion and "data overlay blindness," Orbe maps data points (such as deforestation, sea ice extent, and CO2 levels) to four distinct audio voices and vibrating controllers. This innovation breaks systemic barriers, making climate science fully accessible to 285 million people with blindness or low vision. Furthermore, its lightweight, browser-based architecture ensures anyone can explore the Earth's vital signs through hearing and touch in a 360° spatial environment.
details:
• What it does & How it works: Orbe is an Earth jukebox you stand inside, translating three climate records into music and touch using WebXR. Users select environments (Rainforest, Sea Ice, Greenhouse Gases) and turn a kinetic 3D sphere to travel through time. A real-time deterministic algorithm maps yearly data values to four vital signs (vitality, diversity, stability, pressure), which drive four audio voices (bass, melody, pulse, chant) using acoustic ecology. No pre-recorded audio is used. The controllers act as tactile guides: the right hand vibrates according to the year currently playing, while the left hand pulses to the baseline of the intact ecosystem.
  • Benefits & Impact: Orbe eliminates visual exclusion, creating an inclusive educational climate lab for 285 million visually impaired individuals. Users perceive ecological damage via sensory subtraction—as ecosystems decline, audio layers literally drop out. This also solves "data overlay blindness," making complex variables readable through polyphonic sound.
  • Scalability: The tactile and acoustic interface can evolve into "Zero-Visibility" navigation systems for astronauts in dark terrains. Astronomically, the JavaScript engine can adapt to process FITS databases or light curves from JWST or BRITE-Constellation missions.
  • Tools, Languages, & Software: The platform runs natively in the browser (no downloads). Tools include three.js for 3D spatial rendering, JavaScript (Web Audio API) for the procedural sound engine, Fable (Claude) to structure the synthesizer, and Blender (assisted by Argon and Antigravity) for modeling the responsive 3D mesh.
